pairs.question: Cur illi etiam Iuno uxor adiungitur, quae dicatur "soror et coniux"?
pairs.answer: Quia Iouem in aethere accipimus, in aere Iunonem, et haec duo elementa coniuncta sunt, alterum superius, alterum inferius.
pairs.derivation: Augustine poses the question and reports the pagan answer. Framing 'inquiunt' (in 'Quia Iouem, inquiunt, in aethere...') dropped as speech-tag. Answer ends at its first full stop ('inferius.'); the following sentence ('Non est ergo ille...') turns to Augustine's own refutation, so it is excluded.

pairs.question: Cur ergo non data est patri Iouis, etsi non sublimior, aequalis certe sedes honoris?
pairs.derivation: Question (why was at least an equal seat of honor not given to Jupiter's father) followed by the reported pagan answer. Preceding clause 'Ecce fabulis non credatur et de diis meliora sentiantur:' is setup/exhortation and dropped; the answer's framing 'inquiunt' (in 'Quia Saturnus, inquiunt, temprois longitudo est.') dropped as speech-tag. 'temprois' kept verbatim (source spelling). Answer ends at the full stop; the next sentence ('Tempus ergo colunt...') is Augustine's inference.

pairs.question: Quot sunt ergo deae istae?
pairs.answer: Profecto quotquot homines fortunati, hoc est bonae fortunae.
pairs.derivation: Augustine asks and answers himself ('Profecto...'). Answer ends at its full stop; the following 'Nam cum sint et alii plurimi...' begins a further objection and is excluded.

pairs.question: Quid diuersae aedes, diuersae arae, diuersa sacra?
pairs.answer: Est causa quia felicitas illa est, quam boni habent praecedentibus meritis; fortuna uero, quae dicitur bona, sine ullo examine meritorum fortuito accidit hominibus et bonis et malis, unde etiam Fortuna nominatur.
pairs.derivation: Question (why separate temples, altars, rites for Felicitas and Fortuna) answered by the reported pagan explanation. Framing 'inquiunt' (in 'Est causa, inquiunt, quia...') dropped as speech-tag. Answer ends at its first full stop ('Fortuna nominatur.'); the next sentence ('Quo modo ergo bona est...') resumes Augustine's questioning.

pairs.question: Quae sunt autem illa, quae prolata in multitudinem nocent?
pairs.answer: Haec non esse deos Herculem, Aesculapium, Castorem, Pollucem; proditur enim ab doctis, quod homines fuerint et humana condicione defecerint.
pairs.derivation: Augustine asks which teachings harm the multitude; the pontifex Scaevola answers (quoted). Quotation marks (presentation) and the speech-tag 'inquit' (in 'Haec, inquit, non esse deos...') dropped. Answer ends at the close of the quotation ('defecerint.'); the next move ('Quid aliud?') poses a fresh question.
